questions.prompt: You have often praised the poets whose songs delight the crowd.
questions.answer: Vōs saepe poētās laudāvistis quōrum carmina turbam dēlectant.

questions.prompt: The daughters of the king were carried off by the enemy during the night.
questions.answer: Fīliae rēgis ab hostibus nocte ēreptae sunt.

questions.prompt: A great multitude of soldiers were hurrying toward the walls.
questions.answer: Magna mīlitum multitūdō ad moenia contendēbant.

questions.prompt: Thebes was the native land of the brave hero.
questions.answer: Thēbae patria fortis herōis erat.

questions.prompt: Corioli, a town of the Volsci, was captured after a long siege.
questions.answer: Coriolī, oppidum Volscōrum, longā obsidiōne captum est.

questions.prompt: Not every fear is to be considered cowardice.
questions.answer: Nōn omnis timor ignāvia putanda est.

questions.prompt: His only refuge was the ancestral fields.
questions.answer: Ūnicum eius perfugium erant agrī paternī.

questions.prompt: A crowd of citizens had gathered in the forum before dawn.
questions.answer: Cīvium multitūdō in forō ante lūcem convēnerant.

questions.prompt: Two thousand of the enemy were slain in that battle.
questions.answer: Duo mīlia hostium illō proeliō occīsī sunt.

questions.prompt: A large part of the soldiers had already thrown down their arms.
questions.answer: Magna pars mīlitum arma iam abiēcerant.

questions.prompt: Three thousand captives were led in the triumph.
questions.answer: Tria mīlia captīvōrum in triumphō ductī sunt.

questions.prompt: I who wrote these words fear neither death nor the Stygian shades.
questions.answer: Ego quī haec verba scrīpsī nec mortem nec umbrās Stygiās timeō.

questions.prompt: You and your brother have defended the city bravely.
questions.answer: Tū et frāter tuus urbem fortiter dēfendistis.

questions.prompt: We girls were carrying baskets full of grain to the market.
questions.answer: Nōs puellae calathōs frūmentō plēnōs ad forum portābāmus.

questions.prompt: The kid, snatched from the wolf's bite, was hidden in the stable.
questions.answer: Haedus ā morsū lupī ēreptus in stabulō contēctus est.

questions.prompt: The mutiny, stirred up by a few, was quickly suppressed.
questions.answer: Sēditiō ā paucīs excitāta celeriter oppressa est.

questions.prompt: The ships, driven by a fierce storm, were dashed against the rocks.
questions.answer: Nāvēs saevā tempestāte āctae in saxa illīsae sunt.

questions.prompt: The winter quarters had been fortified by the weary legions.
questions.answer: Hīberna ā fessīs legiōnibus mūnīta erant.

questions.prompt: You and I have often read the histories of ancient wars.
questions.answer: Ego et vōs veterum bellōrum historiās saepe lēgimus.

questions.prompt: The crowd of enemies, terrified, threw down their weapons and fled.
questions.answer: Hostium turba territa arma abiēcērunt et fūgērunt.

questions.prompt: The reward of the soldiers was the conquered fields.
questions.answer: Mīlitum praemium erant agrī captī.

questions.prompt: Tomorrow's danger frightens those who trust in the gods.
questions.answer: Crāstinum perīculum eōs terret quī deīs cōnfīdunt.
